accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: We are workshop staff. A mascot is different. It needs a face, a voice, and the confidence to stand next to a 3D printer without asking whether the printer has approved the project.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: The printer has not approved anything.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: I know. The workshop agent, on the other hand, has started deciding which projects are necessary. That feels like the exact moment a mascot becomes responsible planning.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: A mascot will not countermand an agent.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Not immediately. First it needs to be recognizable every time we generate it. Same little weirdo in a picture, a video, whatever we make next. Then we see if it can actually act like a character instead of a logo that learned to blink.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: So you have no mascot. You have a character-consistency experiment wearing a tiny hat.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: The hat is optional. The test is simple: make one, put it in a few situations, and see whether it stays itself. If it drifts into a different creature halfway through, that is useful information.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Useful, yes. For the mascot, less so.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Exactly. We find out what breaks before it starts representing the workshop.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: And what does this mascot represent?

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Curiosity. Questionable judgment. A healthy respect for prototypes that might bite.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: You are describing a small beaver.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: No, no. This one gets a hat.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Well. That distinction should survive testing.
